user.title: Add a Fujitsu air conditioner
user.description: Home Assistant controls the unit directly over your network using its LAN key, a per-unit secret held by the FGLair cloud. Choose how to get the key.

menu_option_descriptions.cloud: Easiest. Sign in with your FGLair app account once. Home Assistant fetches each unit's LAN key and address, then never talks to the cloud again. Your password is not stored.
menu_option_descriptions.local: For units whose LAN key you saved earlier, for example from a previous install or a key-fetch script. Nothing leaves your network. You need the unit's IP address and its LAN key.

discovery_confirm.title: Air conditioner found
discovery_confirm.description: Found a Fujitsu air conditioner at {host} (serial {dsn}). To control it, Home Assistant needs its LAN key, a per-unit secret held by the FGLair cloud. Choose how to get the key.

menu_option_descriptions.cloud: Easiest. Sign in with your FGLair app account once. Home Assistant fetches each unit's LAN key and address, then never talks to the cloud again. Your password is not stored.
menu_option_descriptions.local: For units whose LAN key you saved earlier, for example from a previous install or a key-fetch script. Nothing leaves your network. You need the unit's IP address and its LAN key.

cloud.title: Sign in to FGLair
cloud.description: Use the email and password of the FGLair app account the air conditioner is registered to. They are used once to fetch the unit's LAN key and are not stored.

data_description.email: Email address of your FGLair app account.
data_description.password: Password of your FGLair app account.
data_description.region: Region of the FGLair app you signed up with.

data_description.device: Air conditioner on your FGLair account to add.

local.title: Enter the LAN key
local.description: Enter the unit's IP address and the LAN key you saved earlier. The serial number and key ID are read from the unit.

data_description.host: IP address of the air conditioner on your network (not Home Assistant's), for example as shown in your router's device list. Give it a fixed address in your router so it does not change.
data_description.lanip_key: The unit's LAN key (`lanip_key`). It grants full local control of the unit, so keep it private.

callback.title: How does the air conditioner reach Home Assistant?
callback.description:
The air conditioner at {host} opens its own connection back to Home Assistant, so it needs an address and port it can reach on your network, usually the LAN address of the machine running Home Assistant. If Home Assistant runs in a container, use the host machine's LAN address and the port published for Home Assistant. The unit only speaks plain HTTP, so the port must serve Home Assistant without TLS.

Tip: set **Local network** under Settings > System > Network to `http://ADDRESS:PORT` and new units pick it up automatically.

data_description.callback_host: IP address of Home Assistant as the air conditioner reaches it.
data_description.callback_port: Port of Home Assistant's web server as the air conditioner reaches it.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure the air conditioner
reconfigure.description: Air conditioner {dsn} at {host}. Choose what to change. The unit is checked with the new settings before they are saved.

adapter_unresponsive.title: {name} is not responding
adapter_unresponsive.description:
The {adapter} Wi-Fi adapter of {name} has not answered at {host} for more than 10 minutes. This adapter has been seen to stop answering on the network until the air conditioner was power-cycled. Fujitsu's procedure:

1. Turn the air conditioner off with the remote.
2. Switch it off at the breaker or mains (the remote alone leaves the adapter powered) and wait at least 5 minutes.
3. Switch it back on and wait up to 15 minutes for the adapter to rejoin Wi-Fi. Home Assistant reconnects by itself and this message goes away.
4. If it does not come back, repeat these steps.

If the unit still does not come back, check that its IP address is still {host}. Reserve its address in your router so it does not change, or use **Reconfigure** on the integration entry to enter the new one.
